title: Participant consent/privacy notices and proctoring/integrity disclosures are incomplete or inconsistent

original_titles.title: Consent API (GET/POST /consent) missing; consent reduced to rules acceptance
Consent reduced to a single lobby button; no blocking screen, separate checkboxes or telemetry/proctoring notice; client can pre-accept arbitrary versions
Privacy notice not aligned to DPDP Act 2023; no rights statement, proctoring/integrity-signal disclosure, or prize-eligibility terms
No downloadable PDF at publish time; time and grace rules section missing from the rules document

problem: Rules acceptance is implemented, but a separate consent model for privacy, telemetry/integrity signals and proctoring disclosures is not evident. Privacy/terms documents still contain stale invite/account policy language and draft/legal review placeholders; repo evidence cannot establish that the event has completed legal and operational approval.
impact: Participants may not have a clear, versioned record of what is collected, why, retention, proctoring, integrity signals, who receives data and how to exercise rights.

verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: Inventory data actually collected by code and operations: identity, submissions, device/session metadata, IP hashes, telemetry, proctoring, integrity flags, exports and backups.
Rewrite privacy and terms copy to match the current no-invite/admin-registration flow and the actual four-level code/artifact upload model. Remove stale activation and invite instructions.
Define separate versioned consent records only for processing that requires distinct consent; distinguish mandatory rules acceptance from optional telemetry/proctoring consent.
Add a participant-facing disclosure screen, consent withdrawal/objection path where legally appropriate, contact point, retention schedule and data-rights request process.
Obtain qualified legal/privacy review for the applicable Indian DPDP obligations and event-specific proctoring/prize terms; add tests that published docs and app copy use the same version.

acceptance_criteria: Every data category in production has a documented purpose, lawful basis/consent state, retention and recipient.
Terms, privacy page and actual product behavior are consistent.
Published consent versions are immutable and auditable.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.

residual_risk_or_scope_note: The code review can identify stale/absent mechanisms, but cannot determine legal compliance. External legal/privacy review is required.
